preview_en:
Returning for another cycle in UEFA Nations League (UNL) B, Slovenia will kick off their 2026/27 campaign against a Scotland side relegated during their League A debut.

Match News and Current Form

Slovenia’s third consecutive season in League B will begin under a new head coach, with Boštjan Cesar set to guide his nation through a formal competition for the first time. With Slovenia’s only victory since June 2025 coming during the four friendlies under Cesar (D1, L2), there are some green shoots to nurture as they seek to improve upon their meagre three wins from 12 UNL B games across their history (D5, L4). Winning here will be key to their chances of promotion to League A, and given that only recent World Cup semi-finalists Norway beat Slovenia at home in the previous season (W1, D1), they cannot be underestimated.

Scotland’s World Cup dream was dashed at the earliest opportunity this summer, with Steve Clarke’s men scoring just once on the way to being dumped out of the group stage. Handing in his resignation in the wake of the tournament, Clarke made way for a new era under the tutelage of former Monaco boss Sébastien Pocognoli, whose immediate concern was to help Scotland return to UNL League A following their relegation last season. Playing away from home was an issue for Scotland in the previous campaign, with all three matches in the league phase ending 2-1 (W1, L2), which is the same scoreline as in two of Pocognoli’s last three opening games as a manager.

Head-to-Head History

This will be the sixth H2H and the first since 2017. Scotland will arrive here having never tasted defeat against Slovenia (W2, D3), with both victories coming without conceding.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Each of Slovenia’s three UNL victories in the previous campaign was accompanied by a clean sheet.

Slovenia have failed to win within 90 minutes in each of their last six matches in Ljubljana (D4, L2).

Just one of Scotland’s last five UNL outings saw both teams score.

None of Scotland’s last 12 internationals ended in a draw (W7, L5).

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Slovenia’s Žan Vipotnik ended the 2025/26 season as the Championship top scorer with Swansea (G23), and he may take his time to grow into the game with each of his last five strikes arriving after half-time. Scotland vice-captain John McGinn became Aston Villa’s highest-scoring player in Europe earlier this month (G12) and, in addition to scoring their only goal at the World Cup, he also struck in each of their last two UNL league stage games.

Benjamin Šeško is a big-name absentee from the Slovenia squad with a shin injury, while Scotland’s Ché Adams and Scott McTominay are also injured.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Slovenia’s inferior H2H record may count for little with home advantage against a new-look Scotland, so backing a draw could provide value.

Author: Matthew Billon
